claims.statement: AFIR assigns the recharging service to the charge-point operator, including contract-based delivery on behalf of a mobility service provider, and imposes price-transparency duties on operators and mobility service providers.

AFIR and its 2025 implementing regulation create API and national-access-point obligations for specified public infrastructure data, but they do not create a right to private CDRs, bilateral roaming agreements, or invoice records.
The Commission's AFIR guidance says mandatory participation in e-roaming was considered and rejected as an unnecessary or disproportionate interference with operators' contractual freedom.

OCPI 2.3 already supports bilateral and hub roaming, billing, tariffs, CDRs, calibration-law data, and a CDR object containing relevant tariffs, charging periods, total costs, energy, optional signed data, and an invoice reference.

OICP 2.3 carries session identifiers, authorization identity, start/end times, consumed energy, an optional tariff product identifier, and optional signed-metering values; some evidence fields remain optional, leaving possible but unquantified data-quality gaps.

Gireve directly offers CDR quality checking, charging-price calculation against roaming agreements, B2B invoice generation, payment tracking, and dispute management; its agreement template also defines CDR dispute windows, tariff-history obligations, and invoice responsibility.

Hubject Financial Services processes OCPI and OICP CDRs, covers the EU27 plus Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein, charges CPOs a percentage of payout volume, and supplies CPO-issued B2B invoices with CDR attachments.

Using Hubject Financial Services requires an active agreement, Intercharge CPO onboarding, configured invoicing entities, payout accounts, EVSE assignment, VAT configuration, and authenticated CDR submission; private-feed access is therefore contractual and operational rather than public.
Hubject documents manual reconciliation for full, partial, off-platform, and unpaid invoice edge cases, demonstrating that residual exceptions persist even inside an incumbent clearing workflow.

A credible entrant wedge is more likely to be independent reconciliation across direct and multiple-platform feeds, plus durable evidence lineage, than generic OCPI normalization, invoice generation, or single-hub clearing.
The frequency, monetary value, and handling cost of uncovered CDR disputes among small and mid-sized Polish or CEE operators are not established by the reviewed public sources.
No reviewed evidence establishes that target operators will authorize an independent entrant to ingest private CDRs and agreements or accept its record as dispositive evidence.
No reviewed evidence supports the candidate's earlier PLN price range, gross-margin range, payback period, customer-count path, or founder-wealth timing.

contrary_evidence: [s03-09] Gireve already markets nearly the full proposed workflow: CDR validation, tariff-agreement cross-checking, B2B invoicing, payment tracking, and dispute handling.
[s03-07] Hubject already provides EU-wide CDR invoicing and clearing for a transaction percentage, including OCPI uploads, VAT configuration, and CPO-issued invoice artifacts.
[s03-04, s03-05, s03-06] OCPI and OICP standardize much of the proposed evidence record, reducing differentiation from protocol normalization alone.
[s03-03] AFIR does not mandate e-roaming participation, so a private-feed network cannot be built from regulatory access rights.
[s03-09] Gireve advertises no connection fee for already-connected CPOs, and [s03-07] Hubject uses a transaction-percentage model; these incumbent economics may constrain a new monthly platform fee.
[s03-11] Manual edge cases remain, but the incumbent itself exposes controls for them, weakening the assumption that residual exceptions automatically create a standalone supplier.

Integration and support hours per protocol/back-office combination and the resulting contribution margin.
